richText: A profile is a named set of configuration that can be activated for an application run.
Spring Boot loads shared application configuration and the files for active profiles.
A profile-specific file overrides matching settings from the shared file. Settings not overridden keep their shared values.
Use spring.profiles.active, SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE, or a command-line argument to select profiles.

example.title: Activate the dev profile
description: Create these files in src/main/resources. Run the application with the dev profile.
explanation: With dev active, the server uses port 8081.
Without an active profile, Spring uses the default profile; it does not automatically select dev.

richText: Do not put spring.profiles.active inside a profile-specific file or an activated profile document. Select profiles from a non-profile-specific source.
@Profile controls whether a bean definition or configuration class is registered for active profiles.
Profiles are selected during startup. Changing an environment variable does not automatically recreate existing beans.
A profile name does not enforce permissions or protect credentials.
